builders.name: Madhu Guru
builders.summary_en: Product leaders should map the full lifecycle from market understanding through launch, then examine where product managers spend their time. Uneven effort across stages may reveal how the team actually operates.

keywords.example_zh: 作者把 GTM 放在开发之后，作为检查产品经理时间分配的一个阶段。

keywords.definition_zh: Product managers 的缩写，在这里指产品经理。
keywords.example_zh: 作者建议比较产品经理在生命周期不同阶段投入的时间，观察团队的工作重心。

tweets.text:
If you are a product leader, here is a simple exercise: draw out your product lifecycle.

e.g. market understanding -> design -> development -> GTM.

Chances are your PMs spend more time in some stages than others - because of the nature of your product, your org or their comfort zones.

This is a handoff-heavy, lossy process.

Now ask yourself: using AI, how much deeper can PMs go on every stage?

PMs should be able to
- build a much deeper, broader understanding of users and the market
- iterate fast from ideas to working prototypes
- explore the codebase to study technical constraints and tradeoffs
- run their own analytics and investigate questions as they emerge
- understand the GTM funnel deeply enough to shape product strategy

Now, this is not about PMs replacing every role. As the function that spans the entire lifecycle, this is about  raising the bar on the PM role, so they combine their breadth with much greater depth.
tweets.summary_en: AI should enable PMs to work more deeply across the entire product lifecycle, from user research and prototyping to code exploration, analytics, and GTM strategy. The goal is to raise expectations for PMs and reduce lossy handoffs, without replacing specialist roles.

tweets.text:
So bullish on MCP. Its utility exceeds the "M" part: even AI aside, it'll be a civilization-scale accomplishment to get all our systems communicating through one universal open protocol.

A missing piece was how to get arbitrary callbacks across sessions. MCP could read and write, but it couldn't tell you later "this event happened." MCP Events fixes this.

We're adding support in our own MCP. Say an agent makes a deployment, and wants to know when it's complete. Instead of polling, it can subscribe to 𝚍𝚎𝚙𝚕𝚘𝚢𝚖𝚎𝚗𝚝.𝚜𝚞𝚌𝚌𝚎𝚎𝚍𝚎𝚍.

PSA: With Vercel Queues and Workflows, writing the backend machinery for your own MCPs to do this is easy peasy.
tweets.summary_en: MCP’s promise extends beyond AI to a universal open protocol for connecting systems. MCP Events adds asynchronous notifications across sessions, letting agents subscribe to events such as deployment completion instead of polling.

tweets.text:
At @vercel we got to test this model before release. Best way to summarize it: astonishingly brilliant.

One interesting takeaway: it's very clear that this new generation of models can take on unprecedented bodies of parallel work.

To actually seize this intelligence, you need cloud sandboxes. Full stop. The model can delegate and orchestrate far more than a single computer can handle. Likely far more than you can even imagine it can handle.

Your bottleneck is now ① your ambition and ② your parallel computing power.

Btw, I learned from @cramforce you don't need to overcomplicate it. Install Vercel CLI, setup the Plugin and tell the agent to use /𝚘𝚏𝚏𝚕𝚘𝚊𝚍-𝚝𝚘-𝚜𝚊𝚗𝚍𝚋𝚘𝚡 skill. It'll provision and de-allocate cloud sandboxes as needed. You don't need a "multi-agent remote harness ralph orchestrator" 😆
tweets.summary_en: New models can orchestrate enough parallel work that ambition and computing capacity become the bottlenecks, making cloud sandboxes essential to realizing their potential. Vercel’s sandbox skill can provision and release those environments without elaborate orchestration infrastructure.

tweets.text:
It turns out the advancements we’re getting in coding and computer use, combined with industry specific understand and general reasoning, can bring automation to a large number of areas of knowledge work.

We’re entering the era of autonomous collaborators in a number of industries that haven’t yet had their claude code or codex moment yet. But now this is going to happen. 

We’ll see it in animation, film production, gaming, manufacturing, architecture, product design, robotics, and more. All of these fields have the potential of driving far more output similar to what we’ve seen in software engineering. There’s no inherent finite demand for these categories of work.

“Software is eating the world” is finally in a much bigger way happening because of AI.
tweets.summary_en: Advances in coding, computer use, domain knowledge, and reasoning could bring autonomous AI collaborators to fields such as film, gaming, manufacturing, architecture, and robotics. These industries could see software-like output gains, with demand expanding rather than remaining fixed.

tweets.text: Vibe Check dropping soon: https://t.co/pY1lpUDlOL

BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just dropped Claude Fable 5.2. It’s a paradigm-shifting model if you have a project ambitious enough to give it.

We’ve been testing it at @every, and I’ve seen this crazy explosion of creativity on the team. People are making their own creative software, games for their kids, and documentaries instead of slide decks.

Here’s your day zero vibe check:

• Coding: @kieranklaassen built Everycut, a video editor with the features we use from Premiere, Descript, and other tools—all in one app, with an agent built in. The first version was live in 3 days, and we immediately used it for our internal show-and-tell. This feels like a new era of professionals building their own professional tools, tailored to exactly how they work.

• Games and design: @jackcheng gave it a photo of his toddler’s messy playroom. It turned the actual toys into a playable racing game, with fun details like a stray shoe as an obstacle and a sippy cup as a power-up.

• Knowledge work: @hammer_mt turned his research into a documentary. The model came up with interview questions, he answered them on camera, and it cut the footage together. He called this the most productive 3 weeks of his career.

• A different way of working: Give it a big job and leave it running overnight or over a weekend. But tell it what “done” means: Mike found it could finish the build, then spend another day or two testing. Set the goal, the budget, and how much checking you need before walking away.

• The catch: It’s slow and burns through tokens. Our early-access usage was free, and these projects would have been expensive at API rates. It’s 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1, but for everyday writing, emails, or quick back-and-forth coding, I’d usually reach for something else.

The clearest signal: When our early access ended, @TylerNishida stopped working on some projects until he could get this model back. He didn’t want to build them with anything else.

The best measure of a new model is whether it makes you try things you wouldn’t have tried before.

Fable 5.2 absolutely does that.

Here’s our full day-zero Vibe Check:

On the exact limit of a technique used to rule out candidate theories of quantum gravity: https://t.co/TwAyTW9Jxw

podcasts.name: Latent Space
podcasts.title: What Frontier Labs Buy: A Data Deep Dive with Handshake AI — Garrett Lord & Team
podcasts.summary_en: The discussion projects rapid growth for an AI market but argues that reliable interpretation of basic images must come before more ambitious medical claims. In high-stakes workflows, a 95% accurate output can still fail to save time if correcting errors takes as much effort as doing the work.
podcasts.summary_zh: 讨论预测某个 AI 市场将快速增长，但认为在谈论更宏大的医疗突破前，模型得先可靠地解读基础图像。在高风险流程中，即使输出有 95% 的准确率，纠错成本也可能抵消节省的时间。

vocab.definition_en: Available but not yet used or fully explored.
vocab.definition_zh: 尚未开发或充分利用的。
vocab.example_en: Your subscription may offer untapped value through features you rarely use.
vocab.example_zh: 你很少使用的功能可能蕴藏着订阅服务中尚未发掘的价值。

vocab.definition_en: Speaking words so that a person or device can write them down.
vocab.definition_zh: 口述；让他人或设备将说出的话记录成文字。
vocab.example_en: She uses dictation to draft messages while walking.
vocab.example_zh: 她走路时用语音输入起草消息。

vocab.definition_en: The process of converting speech or recorded audio into written text.
vocab.definition_zh: 将语音或录音转换为文字的过程；转写。
vocab.example_en: Accurate transcription makes voice input more useful.
vocab.example_zh: 准确的转写让语音输入更实用。

vocab.definition_en: The transfer of work, information, or responsibility to another person or team.
vocab.definition_zh: 将工作、信息或责任移交给另一个人或团队。
vocab.example_en: Each handoff between teams can introduce delays.
vocab.example_zh: 团队之间的每一次交接都可能造成延误。

vocab.definition_en: Involving the loss of information; here, describing a workflow that loses context during transfers.
vocab.definition_zh: 有信息损失的；此处指工作交接时会丢失背景信息或细节。
vocab.example_en: A brief summary can be a lossy way to communicate user research.
vocab.example_zh: 用简短摘要传达用户研究结果，可能会损失一些信息。

vocab.definition_en: To repeat a process, improving the result through successive versions.
vocab.definition_zh: 迭代；通过反复修改逐步改进。
vocab.example_en: The team can iterate on a prototype after each user interview.
vocab.example_zh: 团队可以在每次用户访谈后迭代原型。

vocab.definition_en: A series of presentations in different locations, often used to attract investors before a public offering.
vocab.definition_zh: 路演；在不同地点进行的一系列推介活动，常用于上市前吸引投资者。
vocab.example_en: The company prepared an investor presentation for its IPO roadshow.
vocab.example_zh: 公司为首次公开募股路演准备了投资者演示材料。

quote.text_en: Every handoff is an opportunity to ask what could be understood more deeply.
quote.text_zh: 每一次交接，都是追问如何理解得更深入的机会。
quote.author: Original reflection

slang_glossary.definition_en: Go-to-market: the plan and activities for bringing a product to customers.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: Go-to-market 的缩写，指将产品推向市场并触达客户的策略与行动。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Building software mainly by describing desired results to AI and guiding its generated code.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 主要通过向 AI 描述需求并引导其生成代码来开发软件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Model Context Protocol: a protocol for connecting AI applications to tools and data sources.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 模型上下文协议，用于连接 AI 应用与工具、数据源。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI model near the leading edge of capabilities at a given time.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在某一时期能力处于前沿水平的 AI 模型。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A sudden, substantial jump in performance rather than gradual progress.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 性能突然出现大幅跃升，而非缓慢改善。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A research manuscript shared publicly before formal peer review.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 正式同行评审前公开分享的研究论文稿件，即预印本。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal way to address or refer to someone, often expressing familiarity or amazement.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「哥们」「兄弟」；也常用于表达惊讶或熟络的语气。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for demonstration: a presentation showing what a product can do.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: demonstration 的简称，指展示产品能力的演示。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Laughing out loud; often used to signal amusement or a casual tone.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: laughing out loud 的缩写，表示好笑，也可用于营造轻松语气。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal text abbreviation for you.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: you 的非正式网络缩写。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Acting wildly or doing something unusually bold, surprising, or outrageous.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 做出大胆、惊人或离谱的举动；此处带有惊叹的意味。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An abbreviation for by the way.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: by the way 的缩写，意为「顺便说一下」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A ticker-style reference using a dollar sign; the sample does not establish whether it is an actual listed ticker.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 使用美元符号的证券代码式写法；样本文本不足以确认它是否为真实上市代码。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Initial public offering: a company's first offering of shares to the public.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 首次公开募股，指公司首次向公众发行股票。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A series of promotional presentations, especially to potential investors.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 路演，尤其指面向潜在投资者的一系列推介活动。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Had something prepared and ready to release or use.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 早已准备好某项成果，随时可以发布或拿出来用。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In this subscription context, a replenishment or restart of a usage allowance.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在订阅服务语境中，指使用额度的恢复或重新计数。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A remotely hosted computer accessed over the internet.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 通过互联网访问、运行在远程服务器上的计算机。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Public service announcement; online, a useful tip or notice shared with others.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: public service announcement 的缩写；网络中常指向大家分享的实用提醒。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal spoken or written form of want to.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: want to 的非正式口语或书面形式，意为「想要」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Voice input available across applications or system text fields.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 可跨应用或在系统文本输入位置使用的语音输入功能。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Happening or available within a particular application.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在某个应用内部发生或提供的。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The processing pipeline that converts speech into text.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 将语音转换为文字的处理流程。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The stages a product passes through; here, from market understanding to launch activities.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 产品生命周期；此处指从市场理解、设计、开发到推向市场的各阶段。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Product managers in this context.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 此处指产品经理，英文为 product managers。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal abbreviation for organization.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: organization 的简称，指组织或公司。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Requiring many transfers of work or responsibility between people or teams.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 需要在人或团队之间频繁交接工作的。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Losing information or context during a process or transfer.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在处理或传递过程中丢失信息或上下文的。

slang_glossary.definition_en: To improve something through repeated cycles of building, testing, and revision.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 通过反复构建、测试和修改来改进，即「迭代」。
